messages.content: You are planning one day for a resident of the Penn campus. Plan in character, grounded in who they are and what they remember.

I am Diego Torres, 24, a graduate student in architecture at Penn. I am creative, focused, and always sketching. I spend long hours in the Meyerson Hall studio.
This simulation runs from 08:00 to 20:00 today; plan only that window.
You remember:
- Plan: go to Meyerson Hall and working on a studio model. Today's stops: working on a studio model at Meyerson Hall, then studying precedents in the gallery exhibits at Van Pelt — Kamin Gallery, then researching precedents for a project at Van Pelt — Digital Scholarship Exchange, then attending a guest lecture at Irvine Auditorium, then refining the model at Meyerson Hall.
- There's a guest lecture on gravitational waves at Irvine Auditorium at 10:00, hosted by Professor Tanaka. It's open to anyone.
- I know Professor Tanaka: lecture regular. We know each other a little. Diego sits in on Professor Tanaka's public guest lectures at Irvine whenever architecture and physics cross paths; she knows him by name from the question line.
Sketch your day as a few broad blocks.

tool.name: day_outline
tool.description: Sketch the day as 4-6 broad blocks. No exact times yet.

blocks.description: Each item is a JSON object, not a string.

blocks.label: morning
blocks.summary: Arrive early at Meyerson Hall studio to work on the studio model—cutting and assembling components while the space is quiet before critique traffic picks up.

blocks.label: mid-morning
blocks.summary: Head to Irvine Auditorium for Professor Tanaka's 10:00 guest lecture on gravitational waves; catch up with her briefly and ask a question in the Q&A line, as usual.

blocks.label: midday
blocks.summary: Walk over to Van Pelt Library's Kamin Gallery to study precedent exhibits, sketching details and taking notes relevant to the studio project.

blocks.label: afternoon
blocks.summary: Settle into the Digital Scholarship Exchange at Van Pelt to dig deeper into project precedents—pulling journal articles, plans, and case studies to inform the model's design direction.

blocks.label: evening
blocks.summary: Return to Meyerson Hall studio to refine the model using insights gathered from the gallery and research session, pushing toward a stronger iteration before the day ends.

hours.description: Each item is a JSON object, not a string.

hours.summary: Arrive early at Meyerson Hall studio; unlock personal workspace, lay out tools and materials for the studio model before the building fills up.
Focused work cutting chipboard and assembling structural components of the studio model, enjoying the quiet before critique traffic picks up.
Walk to Irvine Auditorium for Professor Tanaka's 10:00 guest lecture on gravitational waves; find a seat and take notes connecting the physics to architectural form.
Stay after the lecture to say hello to Professor Tanaka, then join the Q&A line to ask a question about wave geometry, as he usually does.
Walk over to Van Pelt Library's Kamin Gallery and begin studying precedent exhibits, sketching details relevant to the studio project.
Continue in the Kamin Gallery, taking careful notes on material and spatial precedents that could inform the model's next iteration.
Grab a quick lunch near Van Pelt, reviewing sketches from the gallery while eating.
Settle into the Digital Scholarship Exchange at Van Pelt to pull journal articles and case studies on similar architectural projects.
Deepen research at the Digital Scholarship Exchange, cross-referencing plans and diagrams against his own studio model concept.
Compile key findings and images from the research session into a working folder to bring back to the studio.
Return to Meyerson Hall studio and begin refining the model using insights gathered from the gallery and research session.
Push through a stronger iteration of the studio model, adjusting details before wrapping up for the day.
